positions.name: MigrationDecisionPerformance
positions.frame: how is the database migration performed as a settled decision?
positions.why: All three enact the migration as decided rather than proposed: src-1 declares the switch in present-progressive ratification language, src-3 records it as a bolded summary heading, and src-5 pins a concrete timeline. They share decision-conviction and authority-ranking relational reads — each performs a settling move (declare, record, schedule). Tension: src-1 and src-3 render the migration as present-realis fact while src-5 projects it into future-irrealis planning, yet the frame holds both — settling a decision includes fixing its date.

positions.name: QuantifiedBenefitJustification
positions.frame: how is the migration justified through quantified cost-benefit claims?
positions.why: Both assert performance and cost benefits as unhedged quantified claims — src-2 spoken ('10x query performance, lower licensing cost'), src-4 recorded as a bolded summary ('10x analytical queries'). They share claim-conviction, market-pricing relational logic, rational-persuasion/reward power, and competence value — the switch is argued through proportionality framing rather than authority. src-2 carries the cost dimension that src-4 omits, but the frame's read holds both as the same justification move.
